assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Restore default sbatch refusal by removing the new partition exemption: exit 97 violates expected exit 0; the base negative control demonstrates this.

Forward to a different binary, omit or change an argument, or skip the stub: the independently written invocation record differs from the expected executable path and original argv. Expected tuple(argv) checks transparency against independent stub output, not the input against itself.
Remove the refusal check for any parametrized implicit launch: the recording stub exits 0 instead of required 97.
Remove the newly added explicit-partition instruction: stderr lacks sbatch --partition; all nine refusal cases fail here at base.
Invoke the scheduler despite returning refusal 97 and printing route text: the independent stub record is nonempty. Positive forwarding cases prove the reader observes real invocations.

findings.text: blocking: the scan does not consume values of other sbatch options, so argv ["--output", "--partition=all_debug", "--wrap=true"] grants the partition exemption even though --partition=all_debug is the output filename and no partition is selected; similarly ["--job-name", "-prigel", "--wrap=true"] passes, weakening the required implicit-submission refusal; parse actual option/value roles and add recording-stub refusal cases before landing.
